exploration.title: Food Web Rescue
exploration.subject: Biology
exploration.summary: Predict how removing fish or increasing nutrients changes a bounded pond model, then compare controlled trials.
exploration.question: Can adding more nutrients make conditions worse for fish?
exploration.explanation: Algae capture light energy, zooplankton graze algae, and fish can eat zooplankton. Food-web arrows point from resource or prey toward consumer because they trace energy flow; they do not show organisms moving. This chain is one path inside a larger web, so changing a consumer can affect a producer indirectly. Added nutrients can support algal growth, while respiration and decomposition can consume dissolved oxygen. The model uses invented 0–100 population, nutrient, oxygen and detritus indices, illustrative weekly steps and uncalibrated coefficients. It is designed to show qualitative interactions, not to forecast a real pond. Temperature, light, mixing, nutrient form, daily oxygen cycles, species differences and many other processes are omitted.

experiments.title: Remove a consumer
experiments.instruction: Predict what changes when fish are absent. Compare 6 illustrative weeks with fish present versus fish absent. Hold nutrient supply at index 50, drought at 0%, and the algae, zooplankton, oxygen and detritus starting indices fixed.
experiments.observe: The fish-absent trial finishes with a higher zooplankton index and lower algae index in this model. Use the resource-to-consumer links to explain the indirect response, and identify the changed and held variables.

experiments.title: Increase nutrient supply
experiments.instruction: Predict what changes from nutrient index 20 to 100. Compare 8 illustrative weeks while holding drought at 60%, keeping every population present, and using the same algae, zooplankton, fish, oxygen and detritus starting indices.
experiments.observe: The high-nutrient trial finishes with higher algae and detritus indices but lower oxygen and fish indices in this model. Explain why more nutrients do not guarantee that every index rises, without treating the values as a field forecast.

exploration.misconception: Food-web arrows do not show which way animals travel; they point from resource or prey to consumer to trace energy flow. A web is not a ladder where only the top animal matters, and more nutrients do not necessarily improve conditions for every organism.

sources.title: US EPA: Nutrients, algal growth and dissolved oxygen
